chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Salih ibn Saeed, from Yunus, from Ibn Muskan, from Abu Baseer, who said:

I asked him (peace be upon him) about the man who arrives to the Imam when he is concluding (the prayer). He (peace be upon him) said: 'It is not upon him to repeat the Adhan, so let him enter with them in their Adhan. And if he finds them to have dispersed, he should repeat the Adhan.'
ai.seo_question: What should a person do with the Adhan if they arrive late to prayer and find the congregation has dispersed?
ai.summary: This ruling from al-Kafi highlights the practical flexibility in Shia jurisprudence regarding the Adhan's role as a reminder versus a formal prerequisite for the prayer itself. It distinguishes between the presence of the congregation, where the latecomer simply joins the existing ritual, and their dispersion, which necessitates re-establishing the call to prayer. This reflects the scholarly view that the Adhan serves primarily to announce the prayer time to those who may have missed it, rather than being an intrinsic pillar of the Salah.
